description:
FILED s517a (Opus, 2026-10-15) -- the residue of #1747.

#1747 lowers a literal `goto LABEL` into an if/elsif/else/unless branch or a
bare block (Parser2 _classify_nested_gotos / _goto_nested_fire, runtime
p-goto-region; ir-spec §6.4 "goto into a nested block").  Three neighbouring
shapes are REWRITTEN to a run-time `die "PCL: unsupported goto into ..."` at
the goto, where perl takes the jump (probed perl 5.40.3, scratch/s517a/pr/g3.pl):

  1. a target inside a while / until / C-style for body:
       eval { goto W; while ($zero) { W: print "inw\n"; last } }   # perl: inw
       eval { goto W2; for (my $j=0;$j<1;$j++) { W2: print "inc\n"; last } }  # perl: inc
     (perl enters the body and skips the first test.)  Needs a steering arm in
     the loop lowering like the if-chain's `(p-if F 1 TEST)` -- the first test
     only -- plus the loop's own next/redo tags around the entry.
  2. the goto's OWN statement is a declaration, or a declaration lies between
     the goto and the label's statement in the common list:
       { my @r = map { goto L if $_ == 2; $_ } 1 .. 3; if ($z) { L: print "landed\n" } }
     perl prints "landed"; PCL dies "PCL: unsupported goto into a nested block
     past a declaration".  The decl's let nests the remainder, so the forward
     catch would cut its scope; the #126 decl-hoist (`_goto_hoist_decls`) is
     the likely route for the scalar subset.
  3. a target inside a do / eval / map block.

perl 5.40 deprecates all of it ("Use of \"goto\" to jump into a construct is
deprecated, and will become fatal in Perl 5.42"); PCL prints no warning.
not-supported.md "goto into a nested block: the shapes PCL does not lower".
subject: goto into a nested block: while/until/C-for bodies, a declaration on the way, do/eval/map blocks still die PCL-unsupported where perl jumps (#1747 residue)
